title: Refinement shares its coin, accretion must carry it
claim: Two-kind knot spheres (co-lines of two or three points); K_m the octahedral knot sphere. (1) Refinement: subdividing every triangle of K_m into j^2 gives K_{jm} (j = 2, 3); a refinement step is all-or-nothing in every order, since a split edge forces both its triangles to split; it maps a capped tube to a capped tube, so it keeps the seed's shape and never places a corner. (2) Ring accretion around a corner (each ring vertex completed to degree 6, or a convex turn made a corner): making the four turns of ring m corners gives exactly K_m, and K_m arises only that way. (3) With each turn decided on its own, ring accretion also closes into non-round two-kind spheres. (4) In single-strip accretion the radius-w window at which a turn is decided is the same in every lap of ring at least w + 1, so a label-free rule cannot tie the four equator turns together; one bit kept for one lap does, but that bit is history supplied by the process, a hidden witness under the canonical test. (5) The window law of one order, run in random orders, closes only small round spheres or is stuck.
failure_conditions: A subdivision of K_m that is not K_{jm}, or a partial refinement that is a closed two-kind surface.
A ring-accretion choice pattern other than the four turns of one ring that closes into some K_m.
No closed non-round sphere from independent turn decisions.
Two laps of single-strip accretion in which the decision windows at a turn differ (for ring at least w + 1).
foundation_claim_scope: Refinement by proof, checked for m <= 4, j = 2, 3, and on two tubes. Ring accretion: uniform choices for m <= 6; every choice pattern up to 100 triangles; 400 random-coin runs. Single-strip decision windows for w <= 5 and m from w + 2 to w + 5. The window law: radius 5, from K_1..K_10, 200 random-order runs.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the repository owner's request on 2026-11-07.
validation.status: by hand, with the finite claims checked by computation with controls; no human or external review
validation.novelty: known-with-delta: decorated versus undecorated local rules (Levitov 1988; Mozes 1989; Goodman-Strauss 1998; sofic versus finite-type), local growth rules that stall without non-local information (Onoda, Steinhardt, DiVincenzo and Socolar 1988), local-rule capsid assembly with conformational states (Berger, Shor et al. 1994) and tile complexity in algorithmic self-assembly are classical; the refinement/accretion contrast for the knot spheres and the census of lopsided closures are new as far as found.
